verses.text: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.
Yahweh’s Spirit will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.
His delight will be in the fear of Yahweh. He will not judge by the sight of his eyes, neither decide by the hearing of his ears;

but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.
Righteousness will be the belt of his waist, and faithfulness the belt of his waist.
The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; The calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf together; and a little child will lead them.
The cow and the bear will graze. Their young ones will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox.
The nursing child will play near a cobra’s hole, and the weaned child will put his hand on the viper’s den.
They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain; for the earth will be full of the knowledge of Yahweh, as the waters cover the sea.
It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.

It will happen in that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
He will set up a banner for the nations, and will assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
The envy also of Ephraim will depart, and those who persecute Judah will be cut off. Ephraim won’t envy Judah, and Judah won’t persecute Ephraim.

They will fly down on the shoulders of the Philistines on the west. Together they will plunder the children of the east. They will extend their power over Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon will obey them.

Yahweh will utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his scorching wind he will wave his hand over the River, and will split it into seven streams, and cause men to march over in sandals.
There will be a highway for the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, like there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.

footnotes.content: A shoot from Jesse's stock—the family tree of a forgotten shepherd boy. The Lord keeps His promises through the small, the humble, the overlooked. Here the Messiah is promised not in grandeur but in a tender green shoot, life breaking through where death seemed final.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six gifts of the Spirit rest on Him: wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, fear of the Lord. Notice they come in pairs—inner and outer, mind and heart. The Spirit does not come in fragments for Him, but complete and abundant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His delight is the fear of the Lord, not the applause of crowds or the sight of eyes. He will not be fooled by appearance or swayed by rumor. What a mercy—a judge who sees truly, who loves what is holy rather than what impresses.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The rod of His mouth, the breath of His lips—His word is His scepter and sword. He will defend the poor and decide justly for the humble. The wicked fall not by His armies but by the power of His spoken word. Judgment and compassion meet in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Righteousness and faithfulness are His belt—they hold His robe in place, the core of who He is. Not ornaments worn for show, but the invisible strength that binds Him together. On such a One the world will rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The wolf and the lamb lying down together—enemies at peace. A little child leading them all. In His kingdom, the natural hostility of creation is healed. What seemed impossible becomes the deepest truth: that unity under His reign is more real than the violence we know now.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The lion eating straw like the ox—the fierce becomes gentle, the hunter becomes herbivore. No more killing, no more fear. The predator's nature is transformed, not destroyed. It is a vision of restoration so complete it touches even what seems fixed in creation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A nursing child plays at the cobra's hole, a weaned child touches the viper's den—no harm comes. The weakest and the deadliest dwell together in safety. This is not naïveté; it is the world as it was meant to be, before sin twisted creation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nothing will hurt or destroy on His holy mountain—sin's reign of violence ends. The earth will be full of the knowledge of the Lord as waters cover the sea, not scattered like drops but permeating everything. When we know Him truly, destruction ceases.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples—the distant cousins and the nations turn their faces toward Him. His resting place, His throne, will be glorious because it is the seat of true justice and peace. He draws all peoples to Himself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord sets His hand a second time to gather His scattered people—from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, the islands. The first gathering was from Egypt; this is the greater gathering, from every corner where exile and wandering carried them. His arm reaches to the ends of the earth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A banner for the nations, assembling the outcasts of Israel, gathering the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth. The banner speaks without words, calling the lost home. Those driven apart, scattered in shame, are gathered not as punishment but as restoration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The envy of Ephraim will depart, those who persecute Judah will be cut off. Ephraim won't envy Judah, Judah won't persecute Ephraim—the old wounds between brothers heal. What division and spite severed, His kingdom knits back together in peace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They will fly down on the Philistines' shoulders in the west, plunder the east together, extend power over Edom and Moab. The former enemies of Judah become subdued; the scattered tribes act as one people in strength. United under His banner, they possess what once seemed out of reach.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh utterly destroys the tongue of the Egyptian sea, waves His scorching hand over the River, splits it into seven streams so men march over in sandals. As He parted the Red Sea for Israel's deliverance, He will dry the waters again—a sign that the old exodus is echoed in a new redemption.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: There will be a highway for the remnant from Assyria, like the way Israel came up from Egypt—readers today hear an echo in these ancient roads. The Lord prepares a way for the wanderers to return; He does not leave His scattered ones orphaned far from home. As of 2026-10, we are still on that journey toward Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
